extracted.intended_audience: milk handlers, producers, cooperatives, market administrators, USDA rulemakers, and interested stakeholders in Federal milk marketing orders
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and specific regulatory provisions for proposed amendments to Federal milk marketing orders (pricing, classification, pooling, butterfat differentials, and plant/transfer rules) as applied to the Tri-State and Inland Empire marketing areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class I differentials (Tri-State)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class I differentials of $1.55 for the Charleston-Huntington district and $1.47 for the Athens-Scioto district, with a reduction from a 20-cent spread to an 8-cent spread between districts (plus 20 cents for each district through April 1968 at plants listed by nearest city hall).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: Reducing the interdistrict spread will better align prices among competing handlers, lessen competitive disadvantages caused by overlapping sales areas, and could eliminate the need to maintain three pricing districts by combining Gallipolis-Scioto and Athens. Historical supply-demand adjustments (1966) and overlapping distribution/transport improvements justify the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain or adjust pricing districts (merge districts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine Gallipolis-Scioto and Athens districts when a reduced maximum price difference (from 20 cents to 8 cents) makes separate districts unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guided by competitive alignment across overlapping sales areas and evidence of no opposition to merging; proposed change expected to produce approximately the same returns from Class I sales as prior differentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class II price formula (basic formula)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Class II price should continue to be the basic formula price (Minnesota-Wisconsin price series) for the month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handlers' proposal to use the lower of the Minnesota-Wisconsin price or a butter-powder formula price plus 10 cents was denied. The Class II price must be high enough to permit marketing of producer milk not needed for Class I, but not so low as to encourage association of milk with the pool solely for manufacturing or to return producers less than obtainable market value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class II price evaluative criterion (producer return & manufacturing incentive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class II price should not be at a level that encourages handlers to associate milk with the pool solely for manufacturing purposes, nor should it return to producers less than the obtainable market value for such milk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must show whether reserve supplies can be marketed at proposed levels; if lower Class II would return producers less than market alternatives or make manufacturing-only association attractive, proposal should be denied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class II-A price and classification (cottage cheese)
rubrics_metrics.description: Milk used to produce cottage cheese shall be classified as Class II-A and priced at the basic formula price for the month plus 15 cents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: The additional 15 cents reasonably returns producers for supplying Grade A milk for cottage cheese; analysis of skim milk value, yields (15 lb curd per cwt skim milk), alternative supply costs (nonfat dry milk, imported curd), and transportation costs supports that this price will not encourage imports or loss of sales. Price should encourage orderly marketing while providing highest possible returns to producers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Butterfat differentials (computation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class I butterfat differential: 12% (0.12) of the Chicago butter price for the preceding month. Class II and Class II-A butterfat differential: 11.5% (0.115) of the Chicago butter price for the current month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These differentials simplify computation and align with differentials used in other Federal orders. Historical averages cited (e.g., 8 cents and 7.6 cents in 1966) and impact on allocation of value between butterfat and skim solids are discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Butterfat differential policy (allocation of value)
rubrics_metrics.description: Set Class I butterfat differential to allocate appropriate value between butterfat and skim milk, taking into account that some fluid products (e.g., fortified skim milk) have higher nonfat solids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lowering Class I butterfat differential reallocates value toward skim milk portion (nonfat solids), which may better reflect the value of fortified fluid milk products; comparisons of dollar values per 100 pounds of milk under different differentials are provided to justify the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pooling standards for supply plants (qualifying shipments)
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for pooling, a supply plant must ship in September, October, and November at least 50 percent, and in all other months at least 40 percent, of its Grade A receipts to pool distributing plants; a supply plant pooled in each month September through March is accorded pool plant status in the following April through August period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals to shorten the 7-month period to 4 months or reduce the September shipping requirement to 40% were denied. Shipping requirements are intended to identify plants that provide regular, dependable service to the fluid market and to deter association of milk with the market primarily for manufacturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plant definition (exclude reload facilities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Revise the plant definition to exclude a reload facility (a facility where milk is pumped from one tanker to another, lacking storage/cooling).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reload points have minimal physical investment and can be exploited to qualify as pool plants, enabling milk intended for manufacturing to share in uniform price; excluding reload points protects orderly marketing and supply for fluid needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pool distributing plant route distribution standards (retain current thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not change in-area route distribution standards for pool distributing plants; retain factors of 250,000 pounds and 20 percent rather than reducing to 100,000 pounds or 10 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposal to lower thresholds intended to regulate nonpool plants expanding Class I sales lacked supporting evidence of harm; official market statistics were used to evaluate Class I sales trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfers and classification (transferring handler reporting)
rubrics_metrics.description: A transferring or diverting handler must claim classification in Class II or Class II-A in reports; transferred skim milk and butterfat are to be classified as Class II to the extent available and the remainder as Class II-A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If operators request, movements in bulk may be classified as Class II or II-A to the extent of comparable utilization available for assignment pursuant to allocation provisions. When transferee order provides more than two classes, allocations primarily fluid classes to Class I and others to comparable Class II or II-A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation rules for skim milk and butterfat (order of subtraction and inventory handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: When allocating skim milk and butterfat, subtract pounds in series beginning with Class II and then Class II-A for specified line items; subtract inventory of fluid milk products at beginning of month; use market administrator announced percentages or handler-specific utilization percentages to determine allocations; if skim milk remaining exceeds producer milk, subtract the excess ('overage') starting with Class II then Class II-A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed procedural steps in §1005.45: specified order for subtraction, use of announced estimated utilizations (§1005.27(k)) or handler's remaining utilization percentages, and definition/handling of 'overage' are provided for consistent allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class prices listing and location adjustments (§1005.51)
rubrics_metrics.description: Class II-A price is the basic formula price for the month plus 15 cents; Class I prices include specified district differentials and locational application based on nearest city hall of listed cities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section lists cities to use for applying location differentials for plants outside the marketing area and provides specific text for implementing district differentials and temporary add-on (20 cents through April 1968).

rubrics_metrics.name: Butterfat differential application to handlers (§1005.52)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute butterfat differentials to handlers by multiplying the applicable Chicago butter price by 0.12 for Class I (preceding month) and by 0.115 for Class II and II-A (current month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restates the computational rule in regulatory terms (see §1005.52) and standardizes handler payments consistent with other order provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations of partially regulated distributing plant (§1005.62)
rubrics_metrics.description: When computing the obligation of a handler operating a partially regulated distributing plant, compute as though the plant were a pool plant, with receipts from pool plants or other order plants assigned classifications at the originating plant and transfers allocated at the weighted average price; include charges specified in §1005.60(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the operator of the regulated distributing plant provides similar reports for nonpool supply plants and allows market administrator examination of records, the amount of the obligation computed at such nonpool supply plant will be added to the regulated plant's obligation. This requires report equivalency and verification access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location differential to producers and nonpool milk (§1005.72)
rubrics_metrics.description: An additional 8 cents location differential applies at a pool plant where the Athens-Scioto district Class I price is applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Location differentials are used to adjust producer payments and nonpool milk pricing to reflect geographic price variations within the order area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for denying proposed findings or requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs, proposed findings/conclusions, and record evidence are considered; suggested findings inconsistent with the decision are denied for reasons previously stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision explicitly denies proposals inconsistent with the record or that would produce returns to producers less than obtainable market value or threaten orderly marketing; decisions rely on hearing evidence, market administrator statistics, and economic analysis presented in the record.
